nodes.description: In the growth plate, GAG content and extracellular matrix space are reduced, proliferating chondrocytes lose their flat columnar shape, and chondrocyte proliferation and maturation are deregulated. Terminal differentiation into hypertrophic chondrocytes is specifically impaired, so the physis stalls at the step CANT1-deficient cartilage cannot complete. This is the chondrocyte-biosynthetic-input instance of the shared growth-plate failure mechanism, with the program stalling at terminal hypertrophic differentiation.

nodes.description: Loss of CANT1 hydrolysis is inferred to let UDP, the by-product of glycosyltransferase reactions, accumulate in the Golgi lumen, where it product-inhibits the glycosyltransferases and reduces the UMP available to exchange cytosolic UDP-sugar donors through the nucleotide-sugar antiporter. This step is inferred from the enzyme's substrate preference and localization and has not been measured directly in patient chondrocytes.
